description.p: A privacy-first desktop browser. Ad and tracker blocking is compiled into the engine, so a blocked request never leaves the machine and the browser needs no per-request callback that could become a browsing log.

Credentials and notes live in an encrypted vault that is never sent anywhere. This Flatpak stores everything inside its own sandbox and requests no access to your home directory; file choices go through the desktop portal, so the browser is handed the one file you picked.
Fingerprint Divergence is free, permanently, and on by default. Turning its noise off for named sites is free with it; that used to ask for a Premium license and no longer does.

A page saved with Deep Recall can now be opened and looked at, not only searched, with zoom from a quarter size up to four times. Its picture stays encrypted on this device and is shown one at a time; locking the vault takes it off screen. On Windows the picture now covers the whole page rather than the part that was on screen.

Reading text out of pictures is far better at finding it. A saved page used to be squashed into one small square before the reader looked at it, which left ordinary body text too small to see, and each line it did find was crushed sideways to fit a fixed width. Pages are now read in overlapping pieces at their real size, and a long line is read in sections split at the spaces between words.

Page integrity, Deep Recall and the image check share one window with three tabs, and both of the last two can now be reached from the command palette with Ctrl+K. The image check says which seven things it looks for and can show you everything it read.

Private Tunnel is one click. Apply and restart closes the browser and brings it back at your vault; unlock it and the tunnel starts carrying traffic and your tabs reopen. If any cannot be set aside, the browser now says so before it restarts rather than after, and any it cannot reopen are waiting in the Bookmark Manager under "Before tunnel restart", which is no longer deleted once a restore finishes.

A locked vault says so instead of reporting a broken tunnel, and a tunnel that is genuinely carrying traffic no longer raises that warning when the vault locks behind it. The vault, tunnel and password buttons glow while each one is live. The unlock pane lists what unlocking turns back on.

A saved password now fills forms that used to refuse it and make you retype, and when a page offers to save one the browser names the sender it actually saw. Ctrl+F puts the cursor in the find bar. A new tab hands the cursor to the address bar. The Bookmark Manager can be emptied in one go and counts every folder it is about to remove. A pinned shortcut shows the logo.

Opening a page over plain HTTP asks first, the warning cannot be relabeled underneath you between reading it and answering, and a site reached on a port can now be continued past. A page that offers you a file cannot disguise what type it is by writing the name backwards. On a network that inspects traffic, updates keep working and the browser tells you the network is inspecting.

Private Tunnel is one click. Apply and restart closes the browser and brings it back at your vault; unlock it and the tunnel starts carrying traffic and your tabs reopen. If anything goes wrong they are waiting in the Bookmark Manager under "Before tunnel restart". The panel now walks through the setup a step at a time instead of describing it.

A locked vault says so. With the tunnel switched on and the vault still locked, the browser used to report the tunnel as down, which sent people looking for a broken connection; it now says the vault holds the configuration and offers to open it. The unlock pane lists what unlocking turns back on.
The vault, Private Tunnel and password buttons glow while each one is genuinely live, so a tunnel left running is visible at a glance.

A saved password now fills forms that used to refuse it and make you retype, and when a page offers to save one the browser names the sender it actually saw. Ctrl+F puts the cursor in the find bar, so you can type straight away. A new tab hands the cursor to the address bar. The Bookmark Manager can be emptied in one go, and says exactly what that removes before it does it. A pinned shortcut shows the logo, because the program finally carries one.

Opening a page over plain HTTP asks first, and the warning cannot be relabelled underneath you between reading it and answering. A page that offers you a file cannot disguise what type it is by writing the name backwards. On a network that inspects traffic, updates keep working and the browser tells you the network is inspecting.

The tab pack: Multi-Tab Search finds a word across every open tab and shows a snippet from each; the Tab Switcher finds a tab by a few letters of its title or address; Batch Tab Actions select several tabs and close, bookmark, or shelve them together. These three ask for a Premium license from day one and unlock when Premium launches. Bookmark Search in the Library is free and ranks the closest match first, even with letters missing.

Text Capture reads the text inside a box you drag on the page. Deep Recall keeps the pages you choose to save and finds them later by a word you remember. Divergence Exceptions turn fingerprint noise off for named sites; Fingerprint Divergence itself is switched on for everyone in this release. In the separate PATANYX-Premium build, Copy Compare asks a contact whether their download hashes the same as yours, and Change Cross-Check asks whether a page changed for them too. All of these ask for a Premium license from day one.

Cookies can be cleared for every site at once. Premium controls now show as locked instead of refusing after the click. A Premium license may carry no expiry. The reported host list is refreshed and the wording is American English throughout.
Started without a page, the browser opens PATANYX Search at patanyx.com. A page handed to it on launch opens instead, as before, and new tabs stay blank.

The accent color now frames the whole window and tints the tab strip, toolbar and address bar; on Windows 11 the title bar and the window border wear it as well. The browser's own scrollbars follow it, and on Windows so do the scrollbars of the pages you open, which means a page can read the accent you chose. The nine accents have names of their own; all nine, and all three chrome color schemes, are free. The feature buttons can sit in a strip down the left edge instead of above the page. A Premium license will activate on up to five devices: one request when the vault first opens after the token is pasted, retried at the next unlock if it could not get through, and checked offline from then on; releasing a device frees its slot, and a license allows a limited number of activations in all.

Fingerprint Divergence is stronger. The sound reading a site can take of your machine now carries noise that varies across the recording and is tied to what was measured, so it cannot be normalized away or worked out by comparing two readings. Silence stays silent.

Divergence now reaches into background workers, where a growing share of fingerprinting runs, and covers the element measurements a site can take of text on the page. The reported number of processor cores and the amount of memory are capped, so an unusual machine stands out less.
Bookmarks can be given tags, and those tags appear as folders. Shelves open like folders too, and can carry a note. The toolbar can show icons only.
Updates now offer a single channel while the browser is a pre-release.

Fingerprint Divergence. The canvas, audio, and graphics readouts sites use to recognize your browser get small site-specific noise: each site sees a different reading, and the readings change again when the browser restarts. On by default, with a switch in the Privacy panel that applies to new tabs.
Release notes now travel inside the signed update manifest, so the update panel can tell you what an update contains before you install it.
Hovering a link now shows where it goes, in a small readout at the bottom left. Deceptive characters that could make a link read as a different site are stripped before anything is shown.

Camera, microphone, location and notification requests are refused until you allow them, and an allowed site has to ask again next time you start the browser. Changing a permission reloads the page, with a warning first so you can save your work.
Pages loaded over plain HTTP can no longer reach devices on your own network.
Copying a link without tracking parameters now also unwraps known redirect wrappers, so the address you copy is where the link actually goes.
The browser warns when its phishing blocklist sources go stale.

Copying a link from the right-click menu works again. On Linux the whole right-click menu works again: opening a link in a new tab, the private and quarantine tabs, and the navigation entries were all doing nothing.
Panels no longer show the page through them on Windows.
The vault now shows Premium Time Left where you cannot miss it, and this build can verify a Premium token for the first time.
Wording fixes throughout.
The photo check now finds text that is too faint to see, like white on white, and shows you what it says. The colour measurement is a Rust port of XLiteOCR, EdgeXene's open-source OCR engine.
The right-click menu works on Windows. It never opened: the engine only raises its context-menu event while default menus are enabled, so a menu built with them disabled was never asked for.
A Theme panel, with nine accent colours and a choice of dark, white or black browser chrome.
Updates can download in the background once verified. Installing still waits for you, every time.
Updates can arrive as a small patch instead of a whole browser, when one is published for the version you run.
Update traffic goes through the private tunnel when one is imported, and fails rather than going around it.
Global Privacy Control is sent, tracking parameters are stripped from addresses, and more trackers are blocked.
Private Tunnel: import a WireGuard configuration and send only this browser's traffic through it. Fails closed, never falls back to a direct connection.
The tunnel row in Tab Activity is measured, not assumed, and says when a change needs a restart.
Banners are no longer clipped when a panel closes; Integrity and Updates are reachable from Ctrl+K.
The interface copy was rewritten in plain language throughout.
The vault locks when the workstation locks or sleeps.
Right-click opens links in a quarantine tab; save pages as PDF with a provenance record.
The malicious-host list has its own signing key and refreshes hourly.
List hygiene: URL-shaped feed junk rejected, bare platform suffixes tripwired.
Unreleased test-build version, burned: internal test builds carried this number. Its features ship in 0.9.55.
Site information and per-site cookie clearing from the address bar.
Ctrl+K opens a command palette for every toolbar action.
A diagnostic report you can copy or save, with no browsing history in it.
A first-run walkthrough of the controls that are not self-explanatory.
An opt-in Beta update channel.
Saved passwords can be offered and filled, matched on exact site.
Ephemeral tabs report the engine's answer, not the request.
A page can no longer close the browser by failing to open a tab.
Updates panel states the automatic check schedule in full.
Not published through the update channel.
First release served over the signed update channel.
Page zoom, a malicious-host blocklist, and encrypted-DNS choice.
Initial packaged build.
Final mark and wordmark.
